title: Low-, middle- and high-income countries
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Global health inequities, covers unfair health gaps between rich and poor countries but never teaches the low-, middle- and high-income country groupings the new point needs, so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Low-, middle- and high-income countries
card: Countries are grouped by how much income they earn per person: low, middle or high.
Higher-income countries usually have stronger health care and more access to education. Their people often have longer life expectancy.
Infrastructure, such as roads, clean water, sanitation and electricity, also tends to be more widespread in higher-income countries.
Lower-income countries often have fewer of these services. Middle-income countries usually sit between the other two groups.
draft.remember: Income group tends to go with health care, education, infrastructure and life expectancy.

a.q: Which description is most likely to fit a low-income country?
opts: Limited health services and shorter life expectancy
Widespread clean water and long life expectancy
Wide access to health care and high school completion
Reliable electricity and extensive sanitation systems
a.why: Lower-income countries often have fewer health services and a shorter life expectancy. The other options describe services more common in higher-income countries.
a.clue: Match services to the income group.

b.q: Country P has most people with access to hospitals, schools and clean water, and its people live long lives. Which income group does it most likely belong to?
opts: High income
Low income
Middle income with no services
Low income with long life expectancy
b.why: Wide access to services and long life expectancy are common in high-income countries. Low-income countries more often have fewer services.
b.clue: Many services and long lives point to one group.

a.best: Limited health services and shorter life expectancy

problems.detail: Two distractors do not fit the question or the card. 'Middle income with no services' contradicts the card, which says middle-income countries sit between the other two groups. 'Low income with long life expectancy' adds descriptors when the question asks only for an income group. These options can be ruled out on their own, so the question tests little beyond the card's bare pattern. Use plain income-group options such as low, middle, high and upper-middle.

proposal.title: Low-, middle- and high-income countries
card: The World Bank groups countries by income per person into four groups: low, lower-middle, upper-middle and high income.
Higher-income countries usually have stronger health care and more access to education. Their people often have longer life expectancy.
Infrastructure, such as roads, clean water, sanitation and electricity, also tends to be more widespread in higher-income countries.
These tend to improve step by step from low to high income. Lower-income countries often have the fewest services, and middle-income countries usually sit in between.
proposal.remember: As income per person rises, services and life expectancy tend to rise too.

a.q: Which description is most likely to fit a low-income country?
opts: Limited health services and shorter life expectancy
Widespread clean water and long life expectancy
Wide access to health care and high school completion
Reliable electricity and extensive sanitation systems
a.why: Lower-income countries often have fewer health services and a shorter life expectancy. The other options describe services more common in higher-income countries.
a.clue: Match services to the income group.

b.q: Countries W, X, Y and Z are each in a different income group. Country Z has the longest life expectancy and the widest access to hospitals and clean water. Which group is Z most likely in?
opts: High income
Upper-middle income
Lower-middle income
Low income
b.why: Services and life expectancy tend to rise step by step with income, so the country with the most of both is most likely high income. Upper-middle income is tempting, but those countries usually sit below high-income ones.
b.clue: Which group sits at the top of the step-by-step pattern?
